passage: Teacher's note. Salma, five, held up the picture from the box and said, 'This is what I want.' She pointed to the tower's tip and asked me, 'What goes on top?' 'A small red one,' I said. 'And under the red one?' She traced down the picture with her finger, saying, 'Yellow, then green,' to the bottom. Then she picked the two big blue blocks first and set them on the floor. Mahima, sitting beside her, wanted to begin with the tall ones, so Salma showed her the picture. I only handed out blocks. The tower stood.

qa.q: What went on top of the tower?
qa.a: A small red block went on top.
Salma wants her tower to look like the one in the picture, and she is eager and careful, checking each block against it.

qa.q: What could Salma do if the tower fell over?
qa.a: Salma could look at the picture again and start once more from the big blue blocks at the bottom.

qa.q: How might Mahima have felt when Salma showed her the picture?
qa.a: Mahima probably felt curious, since she wanted to start with the tall ones and then saw a reason for starting with the base.

grounding: Shows a child looking at the picture of the finished tower and asking what goes on top and then what goes under it, so the base blocks are chosen first.

passage:
Gurpreet tipped the blocks out on the courtyard floor. On the box was a picture of a red temple with a pointed roof.
"Bua, I want this one."
Urmila Bua was shelling peas. "Then make it."
Gurpreet held the box close. "Top is the pointy red one." She found it. "Under the pointy one... yellow sticks." She found four. "Under the sticks, the big flat green."
She put the green block down first, then the sticks, then the red roof. It wobbled, but it stood.
"Bua, look!" she clapped.

qa.q: What colour was the top of the temple in the picture?
qa.a: It was red, with a pointed roof.

qa.q: How did Gurpreet feel when the temple stood?
qa.a: She felt proud and excited, which is why she clapped and called Urmila Bua to look.

qa.q: What else could Gurpreet try if the tower keeps wobbling?
qa.a: She could ask Bua to hold the box picture beside her and check each layer, so she can see if a block is in the wrong place.

qa.q: How might Urmila Bua see Gurpreet's way of building?
qa.a: Bua may be pleased and amused, because Gurpreet worked it out by herself, starting from the picture and going down.

grounding: It shows a small child looking at the box picture, asking what goes at the top and what goes under it, so the base is picked first.

passage:
Jin sat on the living room rug in the Busan flat. The box showed a white lighthouse with a blue lamp on top.
"Clara, what goes top?" Jin asked the neighbour girl.
Clara shrugged.
Jin pointed. "Blue lamp top." Jin looked again. "Then under lamp, the round white." Then, "Under that, the long white. Then the big square." Jin pulled the big square block out first and set it down, then built upwards.
The lamp went on last. Jin sat back with a huge smile. "Lighthouse!"
Clara clapped.

qa.q: What was on top of the lighthouse on the box?
qa.a: A blue lamp was on top.

qa.q: How did Jin feel when the lamp went on last?
qa.a: Jin felt happy and proud, shown by the huge smile and shouting "Lighthouse!" 🙂

qa.q: What could Jin try if the square block did not hold the tower?
qa.a: Jin could ask a grown-up for help or try a wider block at the bottom, to find what makes the base steady.

qa.q: How might Clara see Jin's building?
qa.a: Clara may be impressed and happy, which is why Clara clapped at the finished lighthouse.

grounding: It shows a young child working down from the box picture, asking what goes on top and under it, and choosing the bottom block first.
